## TECHNIQUE 

Multiplanar T1 and T2 weighted MR imaging of the cervical spine. 

## FINDINGS 

At the C5-C6 level, there is a prominent 6mm broad-based posterior and paracentral disc bulge. This bulge has increased in size when compared to the prior external X-ray from 2022-09-15 (previously 4mm). There is moderate indentation of the ventral thecal sac and narrowing of the central spinal canal to 9.5 mm, resulting in mild spinal stenosis. Moderate bilateral neural foraminal narrowing is present, greater on the left. 

## IMPRESSION 

1. Progression of the posterior disc bulge at C5-C6 to 6mm, producing moderate central canal narrowing and left-sided neural foraminal stenosis. 2. No acute spinal cord myelopathy.

RE: MMI AND DISABILITY OPINION - DAX VANCE (DOB 04/12/2001) 

To: Julian Vance, Esq. Re: Dax Vance (DOB: 04/12/2001) I am writing to provide my final assessment on Mr. Dax Vance, who was under my care for orthopedic reconstruction of his left upper extremity following a severe motor vehicle collision on September 4, 2023. Mr. Vance underwent complex surgical intervention including dynamic plate fixation of his left humerus and volar plate fixation of his left distal radius on September 7, 2023. Following extensive post-surgical physical therapy spanning over six months, Mr. Vance was evaluated in my clinic on March 14, 2024, and deemed to have reached Maximum Medical Improvement (MMI). While his bony fractures are solidly consolidated, he has been left with significant permanent functional impairment of the left arm. Specifically, he has a permanent 15-degree flexion/extension deficit at the left elbow and a 20-degree loss of forearm supination. Radial sensory distribution is permanently blunted due to intraoperative and traumatic traction injury. He is restricted from lifting over 20 pounds permanently with his left arm. Regarding his cervical spine, he has a documented progression of a C5-C6 disc bulge from 4mm pre-existing (September 2022) to 6mm post- incident (December 2023). This 6mm bulge is now producing moderate left-sided neural foraminal stenosis, directly matching his post-accident symptoms of persistent severe neck pain and radiating stiffness. Given the severe mechanisms of the MVA, it is my medical opinion that the collision directly exacerbated and worsened his underlying disc disease. He will likely require chronic pain management or potential surgical decompression in the future. Sincerely, Dr. Myrtle Turner, MD, FACS 

Sincerely, Dr. Myrtle Turner Dr. Myrtle Turner, MD, FACS - Orthopedic Surgery
